vulnerabilities.title: Lodash vulnerable to Prototype Pollution
vulnerabilities.description: Lodash versions before 4.17.21 are vulnerable to Prototype Pollution when using the assignIn, extend, merge, or defaultsDeep functions with untrusted source objects.

vulnerabilities.title: NumPy Buffer Overflow
vulnerabilities.description: A buffer overflow vulnerability exists in NumPy's pickle deserialization code which could lead to arbitrary code execution.

vulnerabilities.title: Pandas Code Injection via eval()
vulnerabilities.description: Pandas eval() function can execute arbitrary Python code when evaluating user-supplied strings.

vulnerabilities.title: SciPy Insecure Randomness
vulnerabilities.description: SciPy uses weak random number generation which could lead to predictable results in security-sensitive operations.

security_issues.description: Direct use of eval() with user-supplied input can lead to arbitrary code execution
security_issues.remediation: Use ast.literal_eval() for safe evaluation of literal expressions only

security_issues.description: Using pickle.loads() on untrusted data can execute arbitrary code
security_issues.remediation: Use safer serialization methods like JSON for untrusted input

security_issues.description: Using shell=True in subprocess calls is vulnerable to shell injection attacks
security_issues.remediation: Use subprocess.run() with shell=False and pass arguments as a list

security_issues.description: os.system() is vulnerable to command injection
security_issues.remediation: Use subprocess.run() instead

security_issues.description: Direct use of exec() with user input allows arbitrary code execution
security_issues.remediation: Avoid exec() - use ast.literal_eval() or safer alternatives

security_issues.code: query = f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE id={user_id}"
security_issues.description: SQL query built with string concatenation is vulnerable to injection attacks
security_issues.remediation: Use parameterized queries with proper parameter binding

security_issues.description: Rendering user input as template string can lead to Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI)
security_issues.remediation: Never render user input as template - use template escaping

security_issues.description: Using random module for security-sensitive operations is not cryptographically secure
security_issues.remediation: Use secrets module for cryptographic randomness

security_issues.description: Missing timeout parameter in requests.get() can cause the application to hang indefinitely
security_issues.remediation: Always add timeout parameter: requests.get(url, timeout=10)

security_issues.description: Hardcoded database credentials expose sensitive information
security_issues.remediation: Use environment variables or secrets management services

security_issues.description: Hardcoded API keys expose sensitive credentials
security_issues.remediation: Store secrets in environment variables or a secrets vault

security_issues.description: Running Flask app with debug=True in production exposes sensitive information and enables remote code execution
security_issues.remediation: Set debug=False in production environments

security_issues.description: Using dangerouslySetInnerHTML with user input is vulnerable to XSS attacks
security_issues.remediation: Avoid dangerouslySetInnerHTML - render as text content instead

security_issues.code: const query = `SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ${userId}`;
security_issues.description: SQL query built with template literals is vulnerable to injection
security_issues.remediation: Use prepared statements with parameterized queries

security_issues.description: Direct use of eval() with user data allows arbitrary code execution
security_issues.remediation: Use safer alternatives like JSON.parse() or Function constructor with restrictions

security_issues.description: Using innerHTML with user input is vulnerable to XSS attacks
security_issues.remediation: Use textContent instead or use a DOMParser with proper validation

security_issues.description: Using Function constructor with user input allows arbitrary code execution
security_issues.remediation: Avoid dynamic code execution - use pre-compiled functions

security_issues.description: Using Math.random for security-sensitive operations is not cryptographically secure
security_issues.remediation: Use crypto.getRandomValues() for secure random generation

security_issues.description: Hardcoded API key exposed in source code
security_issues.remediation: Use environment variables to store secrets

security_issues.description: User input directly in HTML attribute vulnerable to XSS
security_issues.remediation: Use HTML templating engines with auto-escaping

security_issues.description: JSON.parse without validation on potentially malicious input
security_issues.remediation: Validate and sanitize input before parsing
